For the two-coordinate identity coefficient family and mass z0+z1, both identity and the singular reset T(z)=(z0+z1,0) solve the same match. They are distinct, and (1,-1) is an explicit unseen nonzero direction. The first false control rejects uniqueness without fitted observability.

The template has identity constant and zero linear coefficient; the fit has identity constant and second-coordinate projection linear coefficient. Reset solves the actual match. Empty and one-letter fitted mass rows span the two-dimensional dual, so reset is uniquely selected, yet e0 and e1 have the same reset image. The second false control rejects claiming this unique match is bijective.

Zero-dimensional states and empty coefficient indices introduce no unproved nonvacuous probability law. Same state dimension and same uniform reference are explicit. No statistical estimation, supplied true template recovery, nonpolynomial family, or noisy approximate match is claimed.
